_meta.openai/toolInvocation/invoking: Checking the text for AI-writing habits...

description:
Flags writing habits. It cannot say who wrote the text. Best for: "which parts of this email sound like AI?", "find the filler in my draft" or "does this cover letter lean on stock phrases?".
Returns: up to 60 findings in text order, each with rule, severity (high, medium or low), start and end offsets, the matched words, the problem and a fix; a 0 to 100 score with its basis; the rule source and date. Under 40 words the answer is still a normal result: score null, level too_short, findings listed.
Input tips: send text exactly as written, at most 12,000 characters. Never paraphrase it: the offsets point into it. A longer text is refused with text_too_long; split it at paragraph breaks and check each part.
Not for: deciding whether an AI wrote the text, rewriting it, or checking facts, grammar or plagiarism. The rules are fixed patterns, not an AI model, and the text is not stored.

examples.text: It is important to note that we delve into a rich tapestry of ideas.

text.description: The text to check, copied exactly as the user wrote it, such as "Great question! I hope this helps." At most 12,000 characters (about 2,000 words); a score needs at least 40 words. Plain text or Markdown. Code blocks, inline code and web links are not checked, but they still count in the offsets, which always point into the text as sent.

name: check_ai_writing

as_of.description: Date the rule set was last reviewed (YYYY-MM-DD).

caveat.description: Fixed reminder to pass on: a finding is a place to look at, not proof of who wrote the text.

findings.description: At most 60, in text order. When more exist, the most severe are kept.

end.description: Offset just after the last matched character; text.slice(start, end) gives the matched words.

excerpt.description: The matched words, the text from start to end, cut to 120 characters with … when longer.

fix.description: A concrete change the writer can make.

problem.description: Why this habit reads like AI writing, in plain words.

rule.description: Rule id, such as hedging-opener or dash-density.

severity.description: How strongly the habit reads as AI writing: high 3 points, medium 2, low 1.

start.description: Offset of the first matched character in the text as sent (UTF-16 code units).

not_authorship.description: Fixed. A low score is not an authorship verdict.
enum: A low score is not an authorship verdict.

rules_version.description: Version of the rule set, such as 1. The same text and version always give the same answer.

source.description: Where the rules come from: fixed patterns written for this service, with no AI model.

basis.description: How the score is worked out. For a too_short text it also says how many words to send for a score.

by_rule.description: Findings per rule id, most frequent first. Only rules with a finding appear.

findings.description: All findings, including any left out of the findings list.

level.description: low under 15, moderate 15 to 39, high 40 or more; too_short under 40 words, with findings still listed.

score.description: 0 to 100, or null when the text has fewer than 40 words.

sentence_length.description: Sentence lengths in words, the basis of the rhythm rules.

mean_words.description: Mean words per sentence, to one decimal.

stdev_words.description: Standard deviation of words per sentence, to one decimal.

text.description: Size of the text that was checked.

characters.description: Characters in the text as sent, code included.

words.description: Words in the prose, after code blocks and links are left out.

truncated.description: True when there were more than 60 findings; summary still counts all of them.

title: Check text for AI-writing tells
